why: Tests, correctness, backward compatibility, user value, and surprising behavior need focused review because this changes boolean simplification semantics, including nullable and nondeterministic expressions. The user-visible simplification also merits checking the PR description/changelog obligation.

Required checks include correctness, error_model, and backward_compat because OFFSET parsing, validation, execution, and optimizer rewrites change observable semantics; tests are extensive but must verify fractional and non-deterministic expressions. User_docs, doc_comments, and change_description need review because syntax/behavior and contracts are documented, while contradictions and spec_conformance need checking for consistency with FETCH and SQL dialect rules.

Tests and correctness merit focused review because the new metadata guard controls whether a rewrite preserves aggregate semantics, including empty and potentially empty inputs. Backward compatibility, surprising behavior, and contradictions also warrant focus because the rule now declines a previously eligible transformation unless non-emptiness is proven, while the PR claims safe behavior preservation.

Focused checks are required for correctness and regression coverage because the new validation has special handling for single-column ARRAY/MULTISET and MAP inputs; doc_comments and contradictions merit review because the non-obvious exception is documented only in implementation comments and must remain consistent with Collect’s existing contract.

Required attention is warranted for tests and correctness because this behavior fix adds regression coverage and changes routine matching; backward compatibility, error_model, and surprising_behavior merit focused review because the prior code could reject valid calls. The PR also describes a user-visible bug fix, while the new Javadoc and description should be checked for consistency with the changed behavior.

Tests, correctness, backward compatibility, and spec conformance deserve focused review because the patch changes escaping semantics for pushed-down Pig literals and that behavior is externally observable. Contradictions also merit focus because comments and tests are updated alongside the implementation to assert Pig-specific quoting rules.

Required checks include correctness, tests, and spec conformance because this adds a non-trivial inequality-join algorithm and planner rule whose SQL comparison semantics and edge cases need validation. Performance, compatibility, resource lifecycle, API comments, and user-visible behavior also merit focused review given the new enumerable implementation and planner integration.

Tests, backward compatibility, correctness, surprising behavior, and contradictions require focused review because the rewrite changes where outer ORDER BY, OFFSET, and FETCH are applied and tests cover only FETCH. The title/description describe preserving rewritten limits, so verify the changed merge conditions retain semantics for existing ordering and limits.

Tests are extensive but correctness/spec-conformance review is required because join-type-specific expansion changes SQL ORDER BY semantics, with potential compatibility and surprising-behavior regressions. Backward compatibility, surprising behavior, and contradictions also merit focused attention because common-column resolution and alias handling change across SELECT, GROUP BY, and ORDER BY paths.

Tests is required because this PR's entire behavior change is re-enabling and adjusting regression tests, so a focused pass must confirm the assertions are meaningful and stable. Correctness is required to verify the updated plan and metadata expectation match actual optimizer behavior rather than merely making formerly disabled assertions pass.

Tests and correctness require focused review because the validator changes common-column expansion in roll-up checking and the added cases cover identifier expansion modes. Backward compatibility is required because this fixes previously failing valid JOIN USING/NATURAL queries, so reviewers should verify both old and new validation behavior.

Focused review is required for correctness, security, and SQL-spec conformance because string and identifier escaping changes span multiple dialect grammars and adapter-generated queries; backward compatibility, surprising behavior, and user value also need review due to a new default system property and changed SQL output. Tests, user documentation, the PR description/changelog, and contradictions require focused attention because the change is broad and introduces user-visible escaping behavior and configuration.

Focused checks are required for tests, build_ci, backward_compat, correctness, user_docs, user_value, surprising_behavior, and contradictions because the change alters compiler/runtime separation, CI JDK provisioning, the default build JDK and release target, and documents claims that need to match actual behavior. Split the review to validate Gradle/toolchain and CI interactions separately from user-facing compatibility and documentation claims.

Required axes are tests, doc_comments, performance, backward_compat, error_model, correctness, user_value, surprising_behavior, contradictions, and spec_conformance: this changes InputStream-visible semantics and adds seek/limit/error paths, while adding public API and nontrivial behavior that needs contract and regression checks.

Tests, correctness, and contradictions deserve focused review because many runtime message translations are newly populated and placeholder fidelity or stale fuzzy entries could affect emitted diagnostics; the generated catalogue and attribution also warrant checking for consistency. Other touched axes need only a glance; no separate specialist pass is indicated.

Tests, backward compatibility, correctness, and user value require focused review because the change creates hundreds of user-facing legacy URL redirects whose coverage, destinations, and static-site behavior must be verified. Contradictions also merit a focused check that the claimed alias coverage and generated redirect behavior match the front matter and build.

Required checks are tests and correctness because the new dynamic-matrix upload/fallback and notification flow need regression and failure-path validation; security and build_ci because the workflow commits a Codecov token and substantially changes CI behavior. Surprising_behavior and contradictions also need focused review because the token/fork gating and documented coverage behavior are user-visible, and portions of the description and workflow comments appear inconsistent with the actual step ordering and report behavior.

Tests and correctness need focused review because this behavioral fix changes the close/flush ordering, including repeated close and flush-failure paths. Error-model review is also required because the ordering changes whether writes can throw during close and how failures affect the object's closed state.

Required checks include tests, user documentation, doc comments, backward compatibility, error behavior, correctness, user value, surprising behavior, contradictions, and PostgreSQL spec conformance: this changes cache invalidation based on a server-reported parameter status and claims version-dependent behavior. The added test and docs also require checking that the described pre-18 failure and PostgreSQL 18+ behavior actually match the driver and server semantics.

The release entry is user-visible and therefore needs a focused check that the changelog and release description are complete and accurate. Contradictions merit focused review because the change duplicates release notes across files, renames the prior release entry, and the submitted diff is truncated.

Focused checks are required for tests, security, backward compatibility, error handling, correctness, surprising behavior, and spec conformance because this changes SCRAM channel-binding negotiation and deliberately rejects formerly accepted connections under `require`. The added regression tests and new failure paths should be checked to ensure they verify the downgrade prevention and report actionable errors.

Focused checks are owed for tests, user docs, change description, backward compatibility, error model, correctness, surprising behavior, and contradictions: the implementation only adds a guard in one parsing method and tests only `toTimestamp`, despite the description claiming broader coverage. The PR also changes the reported error for empty input, so verify the intended user-facing behavior and any required release documentation.

Security and build_ci are required because this updates a pinned third-party action across workflows, including credential-writing and release/automation contexts, so the new revision and workflow compatibility warrant focused verification. Tests, compatibility, and other workflow semantics merit only a glance because the change is a mechanical pin update.

Tests is required because the PR adds regression coverage for JDBC metadata defaults, so a focused check of the test setup and assertions is owed. The other axes are limited to glances over the helper’s result handling and consistency with the documented COLUMN_DEF behavior.

Required axes are tests, doc_comments, change_description, performance, security, backward_compat, error_model, correctness, surprising_behavior, contradictions, and spec_conformance: the PR changes wire parsing and allocation limits, connection failure behavior, public-facing protocol handling, comments, tests, and changelog claims. The broad set of message types and nested length checks warrants focused correctness/security/spec review alongside compatibility and documentation cross-checks.

Tests, backward compatibility, correctness, and build/CI need focused attention because this is a toolchain upgrade that can break supported environments or the build despite the small diff. The description is present, while documentation and other axes are not materially changed.

Required checks are tests, doc_comments, change_description, backward_compat, correctness, user_value, and contradictions: this is a user-facing generic-nullability bug fix with substantial type-manipulation logic, new public-facing behavior, added nontrivial helpers, and no explicit changelog entry visible in the submitted changes.

Tests and correctness require focused review because this changes recursive javac type-copying and bound traversal; backward compatibility needs checking because type identity and substitution behavior change. Doc comments and contradictions merit focused review because new public helpers document delicate javac copy semantics that must match both JDK-version implementations.

Tests, correctness, and backward compatibility require focused checks because the fix changes how multiple nullable upper bounds are stored and exposes a changed cache API contract. The test targets only BiConsumer behavior, so reviewers should verify other affected type-variable bounds and ensure the collection/API change preserves expected behavior.

Required review is owed for tests, doc comments on the newly added non-obvious inference logic, change description/release-note completeness, backward compatibility, correctness, user value, surprising behavior, contradictions, and spec conformance because this changes JSpecify generic type inference and its diagnostics for anonymous diamond expressions.

Required axes: tests and correctness/spec_conformance need focused review because this adds a large AST-classification check intended to cover many nuanced JSpecify locations, and the visible tests are unusually large; doc_comments, change_description, and contradictions merit checks because the public checker contract and description make specific claims. Backward compatibility, error_model, user_value, surprising_behavior, and build_ci are required because the new enabled-by-default WARNING check, fixes/flags, and build configuration can affect users or compilation behavior.

Tests and correctness require focused review because this changes raw-array type inference and generic method-reference resolution, with broad new regression coverage. Backward compatibility and contradictions also merit focused checks because observable nullability diagnostics and fallback behavior change, and related paths/comments may no longer agree.

Tests and correctness require focused review because three method-signature registrations change nullability propagation, but the diff adds no regression tests. The description summarizes the intended behavior; other axes are largely untouched.

Concurrency and build_ci are required because this edits workflow triggers and cancellation semantics; correctness and contradictions deserve focused checks because the concurrency key must actually preserve master and merge-queue runs as described.

Required review is warranted for tests and user-facing policy/docs/change description, plus correctness, compatibility, surprising behavior, contradictions, build/CI, security, user value, and Renovate schema/spec conformance: this adds complex dependency-update policies and a workflow, and the description is visibly truncated. Focused reviewers should verify the policy rules and alias checks, workflow event/diff behavior, supply-chain implications of floating latest images and action pins, and whether the stated protections are actually implemented.

Tests, correctness, and backward compatibility require focused review because this changes javac type substitution and nullness behavior, including shared-bound handling. Doc comments, surprising behavior, and contradictions also merit focused checks because helper contracts and annotation-precedence semantics changed alongside the implementation.

Focused review is required for regression coverage, complex wildcard/capture logic and its compatibility effects, and JLS wildcard-containment semantics. The user-visible diagnostic behavior also merits checking for documentation/release-note omissions and consistency across the description, comments, tests, and implementation.
